transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… it’s gotten hard to do my job. I clean buildings, and lately just the thought of seeing a rat—especially in trash rooms or older places—makes me avoid parts of the work. I know it’s probably not really dangerous, but I can’t seem to get past it.
Is it specifically the rats that you're afraid of, or is it more about the possibility of encountering them in certain situations or places?

It’s mostly the rats… or even the thought I might see one. Places like trash rooms or old buildings make it worse, but it’s because I’m expecting a rat to be there. I know it’s probably not really dangerous, but I just… I can’t make myself do some parts of the job anymore.
Are there other situations or places outside of work where you avoid going because you might see a rat?

Yeah… sometimes. I try not to take routes that mean going through basements, storage rooms, laundry areas, or by alley dumpsters if I can help it. If I have to, I’ll keep the door open and just rush through it. I’m scared the whole time.
Is your fear only of rats, or are you also afraid of other animals?
It’s really rats. I mean… the thought of seeing one is what sets me off. I don’t have this same problem with animals in general.
Has your fear of rats affected your relationships with family or friends in any way?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I haven’t noticed it causing problems with family or friends. Mostly it’s just something I try to handle myself.
Are there any daily activities or routines that you've completely stopped doing because of your fear of rats?

Completely stopped… not exactly. I more try to avoid certain ways of doing things. Like I’ll turn down routes that go through basements or storage rooms, laundry areas, places by alley dumpsters if I can. And if I have to clean one, I keep the door open and just rush through it. I’m scared the whole time.
Have you ever avoided social gatherings because you thought they might be held in a place where rats could be present?

Not really social gatherings… I mostly avoid places at work, like basements, storage rooms, laundry areas, or by alley dumpsters. If I have to go in and clean, I keep the door open and just rush it, but I’m scared the whole time.
Has your fear of rats caused you significant distress?

Yes… it has. I mean, I’m here because it’s gotten bad enough that just thinking I might see a rat makes it hard to do parts of my cleaning job. Even when I tell myself it’s just an old building or a trash room, not really dangerous… I still get really upset.
Is your fear of rats the same regardless of where you might encounter them, or is it worse in specific types of locations?

It’s worse in certain places. Basements, storage rooms, laundry rooms… anywhere near alley dumpsters. I try to take different routes if I can. If I have to clean there, I leave the door open and just hurry through it, but I’m scared the whole time.
Is your fear of rats ever triggered by something that reminds you of rats, but isn't actually a rat, such as a picture or a story?

Yeah… sometimes. Like if I hear scratching near a wall, or see something move by a pipe, I react right away. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I just feel like I need to get out before I can even think.
Is your fear of rats ever less intense if you know you will encounter one in a controlled environment, such as a zoo?

Maybe a little, if I knew it couldn’t get near me… but honestly, the thought of seeing one at all still gets to me. It’s bad enough now that even thinking I might run into one is making it hard to do parts of my cleaning job.
Is your fear of rats ever triggered by just thinking about being in a place where rats might be, even if you don't actually see one?

Yes… yeah, it can happen just from thinking about it. Like if I know I have to go into an old storage room or a trash area, I start picturing seeing one, and then I just… I can’t do parts of the job like I used to. Even if I know it’s probably just an old building and not really dangerous.
Is your fear of rats ever triggered by thinking about the context or environment where rats are likely to be found, rather than just the rats themselves?

Yes. It’s more the place sometimes… like an old building or the trash room. I start thinking a rat could be there, and then I can’t make myself do that part of the cleaning, even if I know it’s probably not really dangerous.
Have you ever felt a similar fear towards mice or other rodents?
Mostly rats. I don’t really think about other rodents much… it’s the thought of seeing a rat, especially in those old rooms or trash areas at work, that makes me freeze up.
Have you ever felt afraid of seeing a mouse in a similar situation where you would fear seeing a rat?
I’m not really sure. I mean… maybe I wouldn’t like it, but it’s rats that really get to me. I haven’t noticed the same thing with mice.
Are you afraid of any other specific animals besides rats?
No… not really. It’s rats. Just the thought of seeing one has gotten bad enough that I avoid parts of my cleaning work, especially in old buildings or trash rooms.
Would your fear be just as strong if you saw a large mouse in the same situations where you fear seeing a rat?

I don’t know if it would be just as strong. Maybe if it looked like a rat… but it’s really rats that set me off. The idea of seeing one in an old room or trash area is what’s gotten so bad I can’t do parts of my cleaning work.
Would you feel the same level of fear if you saw a large mouse in a situation where you would normally fear seeing a rat?
Probably not the same, no. It’s really rats… the thought of seeing one, especially in an old building or trash room, is what makes me avoid parts of my cleaning work.
Would your fear of seeing a rat in a specific situation be significantly reduced if you knew the animal was definitely not a rat, but something very similar?

Yeah… I think it would be less if I knew for sure it wasn’t a rat. It’s the rat part that really gets me. Even just thinking I might see one in an old building or trash room makes it hard for me to do parts of my job.
